title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — split double question: when Christ satisfied vs when imputed
pass_a_gloss: The improper phrase 'when we satisfy in Christ' packs two questions: when Christ satisfied, and when that satisfaction is imputed. Answer: on the cross; and when we believe. Else it is the fallacy of many questions.
pass_b_english: Besides, the proposition when we satisfy in Christ, since it is not proper, needs exposition, and is to be recalled to the proper: otherwise the fallacy of many questions is committed: for it contains these two questions: 1. When did Christ satisfy? 2. When is Christ's satisfaction imputed to us? To that I answer, when he suffered on the cross; to this, when we believe in him.
source_text: Praeterea propositio quando satisfacimus in Christo, cum propria non sit, eget expositione, & revocanda est ad propriam: alioqui committitur fallacia plurium interrogationum: continet enim has duas quaestiones: 1. Quando Christus satisfecit? 2. Quando nobis Christi satisfactio imputatur? Ad illam respondeo, quando passus est in cruce; Ad hanc, quando credimus in eum.
